match.reason: No bank point teaches the flat versus round distinction; the closest, eng-characterisation, is written for Year 11 and covers only static and dynamic characters, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Flat, round, static and dynamic characters
card: Flat
a character with only one or two traits, who is easy to sum up. A shopkeeper who is only ever grumpy is flat.
Round
a complex character with many traits, who may have strengths, flaws and mixed feelings. A reader can be surprised by what a round character does.
Static
a character who stays the same from the start of the story to the end. Their beliefs and behaviour do not change in any important way.
Dynamic
a character who changes through the story, often because of what happens to them. A boy who begins selfish and ends up generous is dynamic.
draft.remember: Flat and round describe how many traits a character has. Static and dynamic describe whether they change.

a.q: Which description fits a dynamic character?
opts: Zara starts the story shy and ends it confident
Zara is shy in every chapter and never changes
Zara is described only as being a loud person
Zara has many different traits, good and bad
a.why: A dynamic character changes through the story, and Zara moves from shy to confident. The last option describes a round character, which is about how complex someone is, not about whether they change.
a.clue: Look for the character whose personality is different at the end.

b.q: In a story, Mr Ellis is a kind teacher who is also easily angered and secretly afraid of failing. He is the same person on the last page as on the first. How is he best described?
opts: Round and static
Flat and static
Round and dynamic
Flat and dynamic
b.why: Mr Ellis has many traits, including mixed ones, so he is round. He does not change by the end, so he is static. Flat is the tempting wrong answer, but a flat character has only one or two traits.
b.clue: Answer two questions: how many traits, and does he change?

a.best: Zara starts the story shy and ends it confident
